text.content: Contigo GmbH's development team is ready to build the knowledge base that will power the support agent's retrieval pipeline. The compliance team has signed off on the RAG architecture. Before any document enters the retrieval pipeline, it must be evaluated against clear inclusion criteria. The question facing the team now is deceptively straightforward: Which documents should actually go into the knowledge base?

text.content: The answer matters more than it might appear. A RAG system retrieves content based on semantic similarity. It finds the chunks that are mathematically closest to the user's query and passes them to the language model as context. It has no built-in understanding of whether a document is current, approved, or appropriate for client-facing use. If an outdated policy document, an internal draft, or a file containing sensitive personal data is included in the knowledge base, the agent will retrieve from it with the same confidence it retrieves from a verified, current policy.

text.content: Does this document contain information the agent will be asked about? A document that is accurate and current but covers topics outside the agent's defined scope adds noise to the knowledge base without adding value. Irrelevant chunks compete with relevant ones during retrieval and reduce precision.

text.content: RAG retrieves based on semantic similarity, not document type or sensitivity level. A client asking about account management could receive chunks containing another client's name, account number, or financial history if that data is in the knowledge base. Under GDPR, surfacing personal data about one individual in a response to another is not a retrieval configuration problem. It is a data protection violation.

text.content: A RAG system is only as reliable as the documents it retrieves from. Including an outdated policy creates a misinformation risk. Including personal data creates a compliance risk. Including unapproved drafts creates a legal risk. None of these risks are visible in the agent's output until something goes wrong.
